notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 11 this time, because the research tool stopped working before I read a single page. My first search returned an error saying I had no tool calls left, and a second try failed the same way.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. With no pages read, I have nothing I can honestly put in the notes. I could write something from memory about what Gill, Spurgeon or Ellicott say on these verses, but I won't. It would break your rules, and the URLs might be wrong.

When the tool is working again (for example, in a new message), I'll run the research as follows:

1. **The traditional reading of each verse:**
   - Enduring Word, Psalm 11
   - Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others on biblehub.com and studylight.org
   - Precept Austin's Psalm 11 page
   - Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or ccel.org)
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** sermons and articles on the main debated lines:
   - v. 3 ("If the foundations are destroyed…"), often used in teaching about culture and society
   - v. 5 ("His soul hates the lover of violence"), the debate over whether God hates sinners or only sin. This could show up on Desiring God, GTY, Ligonier and in Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu.
   - v. 7 ("The upright will see His face"), which touches on the beatific vision
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible translator notes on the hard Hebrew in verses 1, 3 and 6
   - Bible Odyssey, if it has anything on this psalm
   - Augustine's and other Church Fathers' expositions on newadvent.org
   - Any Catholic or Orthodox use of the psalm in worship
   - Popular modern teaching only if these sites actually discuss it

Send the request again, or just say "try again," and I'll start the research.
